subject: Performance SLO p95/p99 - hosted vs current provider - postcall recap
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finlytics.com>; Sam Rivera <sam.rivera@finlytics.com>; Taylor Morris <taylor@finlytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO p95/p99 - hosted vs current provider - postcall recap

Thanks everyone for the conversation today — good signal on both the workload shape and the production constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned before running any perf tests.

What I captured from the call:
- End-to-end latency targets (user-facing): p95 <= 200ms, p99 <= 350ms for your short prompt flows (<128 tokens).
- For longer flows (up to 512 tokens) you expect p95 up to ~350ms and p99 up to ~700ms.
- Throughput target: sustained ~200 requests/sec, with peak concurrency ~40 end users (roughly ~160 concurrent model requests when accounting for fan-out).
- Streaming requirement: partial token delivery matters for UI responsiveness — want first partial tokens within ~50ms of model start and steady partial updates.
- Current provider metrics you shared (end-to-end): p95 ~420ms, p99 ~920ms on average (these include network, frontend render, and model inference).

Open questions / clarifications we asked for:
1) Can you confirm the average token lengths for the two primary flows (short vs long) and typical batch sizes you see at peak?
2) Will all traffic be on a single model or multiple model variants (prompt/template differences)?
3) Are there any per-request pre or post-processing steps in your frontend that we should include when measuring end-to-end?

Attachments I’m including: SLO_matrix.xlsx — please add any missing rows (workload buckets, token sizes, tolerated tail latencies).

Proposed next steps (timeline):
- Sam/FinLytics to drop sample traces and a small test dataset into the shared Drive link (by EOD Mon).
- Redwood to provide a temporary hosted test key and test harness; we’ll run a comparative perf test against your current provider and our hosted API (initial run Apr 13).
- Laura/SEs to run two configurations: hosted standard + hosted on reserved/dedicated (if needed) and share p95/p99, throughput, concurrency graphs.

Please confirm the numbers above and whether Apr 13 afternoon (PT) works for an initial run.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
[Attachment: SLO_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)]

From: Sam Rivera <sam.rivera@finlytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finlytics.com>; Taylor Morris <taylor@finlytics.com>; Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO p95/p99 - hosted vs current provider - postcall recap

Thanks Marissa — quick clarifications from our side (summarizing Sam/SRE notes):
- Short prompts: median token length ~45 tokens; target user-facing p95 we want to hold to 180ms and p99 320ms.
- Long flows: average ~380 tokens; acceptable p95 ~350ms, p99 ~700ms (these are end-to-end).
- Peak concurrency: our web app sees ~40 interactive users at peak which maps to ~160 concurrent model requests due to parallel prefetching.
- Streaming: required. We need first partial tokens within 50ms and steady partial updates thereafter — adds tight pressure on tail latency.

We’ve uploaded a small bundle of perf traces and a sample request set to the Drive folder (see link). Also attaching a zipped sample of traces for your perf team to review.

On the procurement side, Taylor is fine starting with a short eval term and a usage window for the test.
—Sam
[Attachment: perf_sample_traces.zip (zip, 3.1MB)]

Appreciate the quick clarifications, Sam — that helps. Plan from Redwood side: 

1) We’ll provision a temporary hosted test key scoped to your account and a pre-built harness that replays your sample requests. I’ll share the key + harness link by EOD Mon.
2) Initial comparative perf run (hosted API vs your current provider) targeted for Tue Apr 13 afternoon PT — estimate ~3 hours of tests to capture steady-state + stress bursts.
3) SE team (Laura) will run two hosted configs: standard shared routing and dedicated/reserved GPUs (if needed) to show the delta on tail latency.
4) Deliverables: p95/p99 graphs (end-to-end), RPS vs latency curves, CPU/GPU utilization, and streaming-first-byte times.

Please confirm you can put the sample dataset in the Drive link and that Apr 13 2:00pm PT works for a 1–1.5h sync to kick off the run. I’ve attached a short perf compare brief for context.

Marissa

Subject: Re: Performance SLO p95/p99 - hosted vs current provider - postcall recap (internal runbook)

Looping back with an ops plan for the comparative runs:
- Test runs: Apr 13–15 window.
  - Run A: Hosted API (standard routing) — measure end-to-end p95/p99 across short and long flows, streaming first-byte times.
  - Run B: Hosted + dedicated/reserved (simulate Dedicated config) — capture delta and cost/throughput tradeoffs.
- Metrics to capture: end-to-end latencies (p50/p90/p95/p99), streaming-first-byte, backend model inference time, batching stats, RPS, and GPU util.
- Test harness: use the shared Drive replay script with your sample traces; I’ll add a harness configuration file to map concurrency to request fan-out.
- Internal owners: Laura (run lead), Aditya (kernel/config tuning for the reserved test), Marissa (customer coordination).

I’ll be on the call Apr 13 at 2:00pm PT to kick off the test and review initial results. Attaching the internal runbook for our SE/ops team.

—Laura
